newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Burundi's Frodebu mulling armed fight against govt.
newsitem.headline: Burundi's Frodebu mulling armed fight against govt.

text.p: Burundi's banned Frodebu party said on Friday it was considering starting armed resistance against the military government if peaceful political pressure fails to restore democracy to the tiny central-African country.

"If the international community does not take action, if the massacres continue and if the military junta remains in power, Frodebu will have to review its principle of non-violence," Frodebu Chairman Jean Minani told a news conference.
He was in Belgium -- Burundi's former colonial ruler -- for talks with Foreign Minister Eric Derycke.
Hutu-dominated Frodebu was Burundi's largest political party before Pierre Buyoya of the minority Tutsi tribe seized power in a military coup in July.
Frodebu and other parties were banned after the coup.
Minani also called for a strict application of the embargo imposed on Burundi by neighbouring states.
"There are violations of the embargo. I have heard that even some international organisations have broken it under the pretext of humanitarian aid," Minani said.
He added that he had been informed that the U.N.'s World Food Programme (WFP) was most often mentioned in this respect.
"The WFP would have transported with its airplane, dignitaries of the junta from Bujumbura to Kigali," he said, adding that there also had been other flights.
"Pending confirmation of these reports, I consider this to be true," he added.
Frodebu also made an opening towards the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) and its armed wing FDD, which is waging a guerrilla war against the Tutsi-led army.
"The CNDD is a partner in our struggle...but they use different means," said Jean-Marie Ngendahayo, member of Frodebu's national committee.
"If our non-violent struggle does not lead to success, we too will take up arms. But now it is too soon for that," he added.
